column1: # Tokens that are simultaneously an English word and a Roman Urdu word
# (SPELLING-SPEC §5.4).
# Columns:  token <TAB> default <TAB> comma,separated,context
#   default  — the reading to use when nothing nearby disambiguates
#              ("english" = pass through untouched, "urdu" = normalize)
#   context  — neighbouring words (within two tokens) that force the OTHER
#              reading. Empty ("-") means the default always wins.
# Keep this list short. Every row is a place where the normalizer can be wrong,
# and a wrong English reading is the P0 failure this project exists to avoid
# (SPELLING-SPEC §5.1). `Lexicon.load` refuses to start if a token appears in
# both english.txt and canonical.tsv without a row here.
token
# `main` is English in "main road" and Urdu میں ("I") everywhere else.
# Contexts are nouns that only ever follow the English adjective.
main
# `sale` — SPELLING-SPEC §5.4's own example. Resolved as always-English: the
# Urdu homograph is coarse slang that will not appear in captioned content.
sale
# `record` is English as both noun and verb, including in "record kar lo"
# (SPELLING-SPEC §11 case 4). No Urdu reading.
record
to
